title: multi-sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics, parity fixes, v1.209.0 bump
author: Eve Chen
release_notes:
- Unify auth and retry behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs
- Improve streaming API ergonomics and unify event shapes
- Parity fixes for v1.209.0 across SDKs
- Version bumps: python v1.209.0, typescript v1.209.0, go v1.209.0
description:
Motivation: Multiple SDKs had subtle differences in auth retry semantics and streaming event shapes that caused client libraries to behave inconsistently in production. This PR unifies the behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, smooths out ergonomics for streaming (single callback/async iterator parity), fixes a few parity bugs discovered in the release candidate, and bumps package versions to v1.209.0.

Summary of changes: consolidated auth token refresh + retry middleware into a shared implementation pattern, normalized retryable error classification (idempotent vs non-idempotent), implemented streaming Event union types and a consistent API surface (Python: async iterator + small helper, TypeScript: AsyncIterable + onEvent callback, Go: channel + helper iterator), fixed header propagation bugs for private deployments, updated tests and examples, and bumped package versions.

Checklist: 
- [x] Shared auth/retry design doc (ENG-4821) reviewed
- [x] Implementations for python/typescript/go completed
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Backwards compatibility smoke tested against hosted API
- [x] Updated SDK changelogs and release notes

Testing notes: ran unit suites for all three SDKs, integration tests against staging inference endpoints, streaming canary verified with long-lived 60s streams. CI initially had a flaky TypeScript lint job which was addressed in a follow-up commit. Manual validation performed by QA team (Riley) for streaming ergonomics.

Upgrade notes: consumers should see the same high-level APIs but streaming event objects are now consistent across languages. In Python the async iterator yields unified Event objects; in TypeScript the AsyncIterable yields the same union variants; in Go the Channel yields the same set of typed events. No breaking changes expected for typical usage; see examples/upgrade.md for migration snippets.
